title: What LZ's data since April 2024 should show: falsifiable predictions for the untouched exposure
question: Given LZ's data from 1 April 2024 to early September 2026 (and to end-2026/2027), what exposure exists, how many high-energy NR-band events are predicted under the modelled background, the L10 best fit with uncertainty, inelastic fits at delta = 300/350/366/380 keV with their seasonal clustering, and the P001 corpus-prior mixture, and which observed counts confirm, weaken or kill the DM interpretation?
headline_result: 884 calendar days since 1 April 2024 give ~6.76 t yr (k = 2.38 x 2.84 at live fraction 0.593); the L10 best fit predicts 2.4 events (P(0) = 9%, P(>=2) = 69%) vs 0.025 for the whole modelled S1c>500 background (P(>=1) = 2.5%); N = 0 excludes the best-fit rate at 90% CL (s < 0.97), N = 2 is 5.7 sigma combined (4.5 new-only) with P(DM) = 0.36, N >= 3 is >5 sigma from the new data alone (P(DM) = 0.86); inelastic delta >= 350 keV puts 59-78% of events in May-July and implies 2.7-2.9 events because the window holds three summers
model_or_mechanism: Poisson scaling of Table I best fit and Fig. 5 background; Poisson-Gamma (negative binomial) predictive; WimPyDD O1 inelastic seasonal rates (1000 GeV) with Fig. S2 efficiency; toy-MC time-clustering likelihood ratios; P001 three-hypothesis posterior; combined-sample Poisson local significance; N=0 upper limits
builds_on: LZ arXiv:2609.02823 (Data Analysis, Table I, Fig. 5 caption, Conclusion); P001, P002, P006, P007; P004/P010 context
